<verdict>INCORRECT</verdict>
<error_description>
The proposed proof consists only of the assertion that additive space-time white noise “acts on all Fourier modes” and that this is “the reason” for topological irreducibility. This does not prove the required statement
\[
P_t(u_0,U)>0
\]
for every \(t>0\), \(u_0\in C_0([0,1])\), and nonempty open \(U\subset C_0([0,1])\).

Even if the additive noise is nondegenerate in the Fourier basis, one still needs a rigorous argument that the time-\(t\) transition law of the singular SPDE has full support on \(C_0([0,1])\). For the linear stochastic heat equation this would require proving that the stochastic convolution has full support, e.g. via a Cameron--Martin/support argument. For the present equation with singular drift \(\delta_0(u)\), one would additionally need to justify that the singular drift does not destroy support, typically through a support theorem, approximation argument, absolute-continuity/Girsanov argument, or a comparison with approximating equations. None of these arguments is supplied or established by the listed results.

Since the whole tropical line is required to lie in \(\Trop(F_7)\), every such level-set grouping must be compatible with the Bergman-fan flat structure of \(F_7\). In the Fano matroid, the proper flats are singletons and the seven three-point lines. No two-element subset of \(\{4,5,6,7\}\) is a flat, and no three-element subset contained entirely in \(\{4,5,6,7\}\) is a Fano line.
